us: Lead ship of the Fletcher class, the largest American destroyer class of the war. Fought through the Guadalcanal campaign and across the Pacific. Fast, tough and armed with rapid-fire guns.
Lead ship of the Baltimore class, commissioned in 1943. Screened the fast carrier task forces across the Pacific and carried President Roosevelt to Pearl Harbor in 1944. Three turrets of heavy guns.

Lead ship of the Iowa class, the fastest battleships the United States ever built. Carried President Roosevelt to the Tehran Conference in 1943. Nearly unstoppable armor and devastating long-range guns.
The first destroyer built for the Kriegsmarine after the Great War, lead ship of the Type 1934 class. Lost in the North Sea in February 1940 during Operation Wikinger.
Sailed alongside Bismarck at the Battle of the Denmark Strait in 1941 and took part in the Channel Dash. One of the few major German warships to survive the war.

The largest battleship ever completed by Germany. Sank HMS Hood at the Battle of the Denmark Strait in May 1941 before being hunted down by the Royal Navy. Nearly unstoppable armor and devastating guns.
Famed for the Altmark incident of February 1940, when her boarding party freed 299 British prisoners. Later joined the hunt for Bismarck. A fast, hard-hitting Tribal-class destroyer.
Shadowed Bismarck through the Denmark Strait in 1941 and fought Scharnhorst at the Battle of the North Cape in 1943. Three turrets of heavy guns and a long reach.
A veteran of Jutland who fought again at Narvik, Matapan and Normandy, earning more battle honours than any other ship of the Royal Navy. Nearly unstoppable armor and devastating guns.
Lead ship of the Le Fantasque class of large destroyers, among the fastest warships of her day. Joined the Allied cause after 1942 and raided enemy shipping in the Adriatic.
Widely considered the finest French heavy cruiser, with armor unmatched among treaty cruisers. Scuttled with the fleet at Toulon in November 1942. Three turrets of heavy guns.
France's most powerful battleship, her main guns grouped in two forward quadruple turrets. Fought at Dakar in 1940 and later served with the Allies. Nearly unstoppable armor and devastating guns.
Lead ship of the Soldati class of the Regia Marina. Lost in October 1940 after the night action off Cape Passero. A fast destroyer armed with rapid-fire guns.
Lead ship of the heavily armored Zara class, the best-protected Italian cruisers of the war. Lost at the Battle of Cape Matapan in March 1941. Three turrets of heavy guns.
One of Italy's modern Littorio-class battleships. Damaged at Cape Matapan but fought on and survived the war. Nearly unstoppable armor and devastating long-range guns.
An Italian-built destroyer leader and one of the fastest ships of the Soviet Navy. Ran the gauntlet to besieged Sevastopol again and again in 1942.
Lead ship of the Kirov class, armed with 180 mm guns. Her batteries helped defend besieged Leningrad throughout the war. Three turrets of heavy guns.
Crippled at Kronstadt by dive bombers in 1941, yet her surviving turrets kept firing in the defense of Leningrad. Nearly unstoppable armor and devastating long-range guns.
The luckiest ship of the Imperial Japanese Navy. Fought in nearly every major battle, from Midway to Leyte Gulf and Operation Ten-Go, and survived them all.
Lead ship of the Takao class, known for her towering bridge. Fought at Guadalcanal and was heavily damaged at Leyte Gulf in 1944. Three turrets of heavy guns.
The largest battleship ever built, carrying the heaviest guns ever mounted on a warship. Sunk in April 1945 during Operation Ten-Go. Nearly unstoppable armor and devastating long-range guns.
